info.description: Agent-native, read-only XRP Ledger and Solana APIs. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json.
info.x-guidance: Read-only XRPL data. Free /v1/* routes and /mcp need no key or payment; start at /llms.txt. Check /v1/xrpl/fee, /v1/xrpl/network/health and /v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary before building a transaction. Read meta.stale and meta.age_seconds on every response.

get.summary: Current payment options of a paid resource, or the price index, without paying.
get.description:
With `resource`, returns the `accepts` entries the paid route or tool would offer in its 402 challenge, so a client can sign a payment before the first call. Without it, returns the price index: every paid route and MCP tool with its per-call price (VAT included), network, asset and mint when paid access is active, and links to each per-resource offer and docs page; outside x402 mode it lists the resources and `payments_mode` only and names no price. Free and never challenged: it is counted in the `cheap` rate tier. In x402 mode the route answers 503 `payments-unavailable` when the x402 configuration is invalid or no facilitator can currently offer a payment; `accepts` is empty only when `payments_mode` is off or gateway (no paid access). The offer follows the facilitator set and its health, so the live source of truth is this route or the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header of a 402.

When to use: you want to prepay on the first call instead of paying after a 402.

When not to use: you only need data; the free routes carry the same data without payment.

get.summary: Slippage and average price for buying an amount of base currency.
get.description:
Walks the asks of the cached order book to estimate the average price and `slippage_pct` (a percentage; `null` when liquidity is insufficient) of buying `amount` of `base` paying `quote`. For an issued currency the issuer's transfer fee is reported when it can be loaded. The top-level fields describe the CLOB; `venues` compares the CLOB with the AMM pool for the same amount (`best` is the cheaper venue by average price, ties go to the CLOB, no routing split) and `venues.amm_status` is `ok`, `stale`, `no_pool` or `unavailable`. `venues.amm` is `null` when the pair has no pool or the pool could not be read; the response never fails because of the AMM. CLOB slippage is measured against the best ask and AMM slippage against the pool spot price (so it includes the trading fee).

When to use: Before placing a market-style trade, to size it against available depth and to see whether the CLOB or the AMM pool is the cheaper venue.

When not to use: It is an estimate, not a quote, and it does not split an amount across venues or route through other pairs. To read pool reserves, use the amm page.

get.summary: One page of an account's most recent validated transactions, newest first.
get.description:
Returns one page of the account's most recent validated transactions, newest first, in a compact shape: hash, ledger index, close time, transaction type, result code, counterparty (when the transaction names one) and delivered amount as a decimal string (when reported). `limit` is 1 to 50 transactions (default 20) and `marker` is an opaque cursor: send it back unchanged to get the next (older) page; it is `null` on the last page and only valid for the address that produced it. No history depth is promised: history depth depends on the serving node (how far back pages go depends on the ledger history of the node that serves the request), and older pages may be slower because they can be served by a node that keeps a longer history.

When to use: To check what an account did recently (payments sent or received, offers, trust line changes) and whether each transaction succeeded.

When not to use: For balances and trust lines, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`; for full archival history, use a full-history node or indexer: history depth depends on the serving node and older pages may be slower.

get.summary: Pre-payment check: can this payment from source to destination succeed now?
get.description:
Checks, before you sign, whether a payment of `asset` (default `XRP`) from `source` to `destination` can succeed on the validated ledger, and returns a `verdict`: `ready`, `not_ready` (at least one blocking reason) or `unknown` (no blocking reason, but a sub-check could not run; never treat `unknown` as `ready`). A missing account is a reason, not an error: this endpoint never answers 404. Without `amount` the amount-dependent checks are skipped. `spendable_xrp` is the source XRP above its live reserve (base plus owner count times increment, from the server state) and the standard fee; `transfer_fee_pct` is the issuer transfer fee when it applies. Warnings never change the verdict.

Reason codes: `source_not_found`, `insufficient_xrp_balance`, `source_line_missing`, `insufficient_token_balance`, `source_line_frozen`, `destination_not_found`, `amount_below_destination_reserve`, `destination_tag_required`, `deposit_not_authorized`, `destination_line_missing`, `destination_line_limit_exceeded`, `destination_line_frozen`, `issuer_not_found`, `issuer_global_freeze`.

Warning codes: `destination_will_be_created`, `transfer_fee`, `high_fee`, `network_degraded`.

Sub-check codes: `source_account`, `destination_account`, `deposit_authorized`, `source_line`, `destination_line`, `issuer`, `fee`, `network_health`.

When to use: Right before sending a payment: to catch a missing or unfunded destination, a required destination tag, deposit authorization, missing or frozen trust lines, insufficient balance and issuer freezes, in one call.

When not to use: To find a multi-hop route or the source amount needed for a cross-currency payment (use the paths endpoint), or to list balances (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`).

get.summary: Multi-hop payment paths and their source cost.
get.description:
Runs a live path search (`ripple_path_find`) on the validated ledger for delivering `amount` of `asset` from `source` to `destination`, and returns the `alternatives`: each with the estimated `source_amount` the source would spend (asset and decimal string), `paths_count` and the computed `paths` as compact steps (`account`, `currency`, `issuer`). A call can take up to about 20 seconds, because path finding is heavy for the node. Results are best effort: `paths_may_be_non_optimal` is always `true`, a cheaper path may exist and the amounts are estimates that can change by the time you submit. No alternative is a 200 with `alternatives: []`. A destination account that does not exist gives `alternatives: []` and the warning `destination_not_found`; a source account that does not exist is a 404. Answers are never cached: every call reads the ledger.

When to use: Before a cross-currency or multi-hop payment: to see whether a route exists and how much the source would spend to deliver the amount. A call can take up to about 20 seconds and paths may be non-optimal.

When not to use: To check whether a direct payment can succeed (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or for the single-hop cost of a trade on one pair (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`, which compares the order book and the AMM).

get.summary: Slippage and average price for buying an amount of base currency.
get.description:
Walks the asks of the cached order book to estimate the average price and `slippage_pct` (a percentage; `null` when liquidity is insufficient) of buying `amount` of `base` paying `quote`. For an issued currency the issuer's transfer fee is reported when it can be loaded. The top-level fields describe the CLOB; `venues` compares the CLOB with the AMM pool for the same amount (`best` is the cheaper venue by average price, ties go to the CLOB, no routing split) and `venues.amm_status` is `ok`, `stale`, `no_pool` or `unavailable`. `venues.amm` is `null` when the pair has no pool or the pool could not be read; the response never fails because of the AMM. CLOB slippage is measured against the best ask and AMM slippage against the pool spot price (so it includes the trading fee).

When to use: Before placing a market-style trade, to size it against available depth and to see whether the CLOB or the AMM pool is the cheaper venue.

When not to use: It is an estimate, not a quote, and it does not split an amount across venues or route through other pairs. To read pool reserves, use the amm page.

get.summary: Pre-payment check: can this payment from source to destination succeed now?
get.description:
Checks, before you sign, whether a payment of `asset` (default `XRP`) from `source` to `destination` can succeed on the validated ledger, and returns a `verdict`: `ready`, `not_ready` (at least one blocking reason) or `unknown` (no blocking reason, but a sub-check could not run; never treat `unknown` as `ready`). A missing account is a reason, not an error: this endpoint never answers 404. Without `amount` the amount-dependent checks are skipped. `spendable_xrp` is the source XRP above its live reserve (base plus owner count times increment, from the server state) and the standard fee; `transfer_fee_pct` is the issuer transfer fee when it applies. Warnings never change the verdict.

Reason codes: `source_not_found`, `insufficient_xrp_balance`, `source_line_missing`, `insufficient_token_balance`, `source_line_frozen`, `destination_not_found`, `amount_below_destination_reserve`, `destination_tag_required`, `deposit_not_authorized`, `destination_line_missing`, `destination_line_limit_exceeded`, `destination_line_frozen`, `issuer_not_found`, `issuer_global_freeze`.

Warning codes: `destination_will_be_created`, `transfer_fee`, `high_fee`, `network_degraded`.

Sub-check codes: `source_account`, `destination_account`, `deposit_authorized`, `source_line`, `destination_line`, `issuer`, `fee`, `network_health`.

When to use: Right before sending a payment: to catch a missing or unfunded destination, a required destination tag, deposit authorization, missing or frozen trust lines, insufficient balance and issuer freezes, in one call.

When not to use: To find a multi-hop route or the source amount needed for a cross-currency payment (use the paths endpoint), or to list balances (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`).

get.summary: Multi-hop payment paths and their source cost.
get.description:
Runs a live path search (`ripple_path_find`) on the validated ledger for delivering `amount` of `asset` from `source` to `destination`, and returns the `alternatives`: each with the estimated `source_amount` the source would spend (asset and decimal string), `paths_count` and the computed `paths` as compact steps (`account`, `currency`, `issuer`). A call can take up to about 20 seconds, because path finding is heavy for the node. Results are best effort: `paths_may_be_non_optimal` is always `true`, a cheaper path may exist and the amounts are estimates that can change by the time you submit. No alternative is a 200 with `alternatives: []`. A destination account that does not exist gives `alternatives: []` and the warning `destination_not_found`; a source account that does not exist is a 404. Answers are never cached: every call reads the ledger.

When to use: Before a cross-currency or multi-hop payment: to see whether a route exists and how much the source would spend to deliver the amount. A call can take up to about 20 seconds and paths may be non-optimal.

get.summary: Will this Solana transfer succeed? A verdict for SOL or an SPL or Token-2022 token.
get.description:
Checks one planned transfer of SOL or of an SPL Token or Token-2022 token against finalized on-chain state and returns `ready`, every matched blocker and warning code, and the derived figures: the raw amount, whether the destination token account must be created and its rent, the Token-2022 transfer fee and the net amount. Blockers: insufficient_balance, insufficient_sol_for_fees (5,000 lamports for one signature, priority fees excluded, plus the account rent when the destination token account is missing, plus the amount for SOL), source_below_rent_exempt, destination_below_rent_exempt, source_frozen, destination_frozen, non_transferable, mint_paused. Warnings: destination_off_curve, memo_required. The rent-exempt minimum is read live and never hardcoded. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the context slot of the read. The amount is not part of any cache key, so the verdict is computed per request.

When to use: Before building or signing a Solana transfer, to learn whether it will fail and what it will cost in rent and fees.

When not to use: Not a simulation of the exact transaction (no priority fee, no program logic), not a token price or holder lookup, and not a way to read raw accounts.

get.summary: Will this Solana transfer succeed? A verdict for SOL or an SPL or Token-2022 token.
get.description:
Checks one planned transfer of SOL or of an SPL Token or Token-2022 token against finalized on-chain state and returns `ready`, every matched blocker and warning code, and the derived figures: the raw amount, whether the destination token account must be created and its rent, the Token-2022 transfer fee and the net amount. Blockers: insufficient_balance, insufficient_sol_for_fees (5,000 lamports for one signature, priority fees excluded, plus the account rent when the destination token account is missing, plus the amount for SOL), source_below_rent_exempt, destination_below_rent_exempt, source_frozen, destination_frozen, non_transferable, mint_paused. Warnings: destination_off_curve, memo_required. The rent-exempt minimum is read live and never hardcoded. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the context slot of the read. The amount is not part of any cache key, so the verdict is computed per request.

When to use: Before building or signing a Solana transfer, to learn whether it will fail and what it will cost in rent and fees.

When not to use: Not a simulation of the exact transaction (no priority fee, no program logic), not a token price or holder lookup, and not a way to read raw accounts.

get.summary: Is this Solana token safe to hold or receive? A SAFE, WARN or DANGER verdict.
get.description:
Decodes an SPL Token or Token-2022 mint (including its extensions) and returns the token program, decimals, exact supply, the authorities, the extension names and a verdict with every matched reason code. DANGER: permanent_delegate, transfer_hook, pausable, default_account_frozen. WARN: mint_authority_set, freeze_authority_set, transfer_fee, mint_close_authority, unknown_extension. SAFE has no reasons. The verdict is the highest level matched. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the context slot of the read. It returns no holders, liquidity, price or metadata.

When to use: Before accepting or swapping into an unfamiliar token, to see whether its mint can freeze, mint more, move or tax balances.

When not to use: Not a price, liquidity or holder lookup and not an audit of the token's project; it reads only the mint account.
